title: Laredo stash house operator sentenced to 151 months after migrant's death
excerpt: Lucas Gallegos Vasquez, 41, was sentenced to 151 months in federal prison for running a Laredo stash house where 32 people were held in extreme heat with little food or water. One man died.
content:
A Laredo stash house operator was sentenced to 151 months — more than 12 years — in federal prison for his role in a human smuggling operation that held 32 people in dangerous conditions and left one man dead.

Lucas Gallegos Vasquez, 41, a Mexican national, pleaded guilty June 3. Visiting U.S. District Judge Ivan Lemelle imposed the sentence Thursday, Nov. 19, and ordered Vasquez to pay more than $46,000 in restitution to the victim's family. He is expected to face removal proceedings after his prison term.

The investigation began Oct. 15, 2025, when authorities found 30 people, including five minors, crammed into the sleeper compartment of a tractor-trailer. Two others had been taken to a Laredo hospital, where one was pronounced dead on arrival. The medical examiner identified environmental exposure with heat effects as one of the causes of death.

Investigators determined all 32 people had been held at a stash house Vasquez operated. They endured extreme heat, poor ventilation and limited food and water. Vasquez prevented them from leaving and forced them to use buckets as toilets, prosecutors said.

As part of his plea, Vasquez admitted he conspired with others to harbor the 32 people at the Laredo stash house in exchange for payment, knowing they were in the country illegally and helping conceal them from authorities.

At the sentencing hearing, the court heard from the deceased man's wife, who described the impact of his death on their two sons and the financial hardship she faces raising them alone. The court noted Vasquez's responsibility as the stash house operator and his failure to seek medical assistance when the victim showed signs of needing care.

The case was investigated by Homeland Security Investigations with assistance from the Border Patrol and the Laredo Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Tae W. Chon prosecuted the case.

The sentencing came as federal prosecutors announced charges against 222 people in a single week, Nov. 13–19, in the Southern District of Texas, as part of Operation Take Back America. Of those charged, 204 are undocumented immigrants, and 163 of the criminal complaints involve felony reentry after a prior removal.

Source: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Texas — “Illegal alien stash house operator sentenced for harboring 32 illegal aliens in deadly smuggling scheme”, https://www.justice.gov/usao-sdtx/pr/illegal-alien-stash-house-operator-sentenced-harboring-32-illegal-aliens-deadly
